title: The two wills: the simple will in the Essence, and the general will that holds every detail in one glance
overview: Chapter 16 sets out to explain the circles of the *Kav*, "it circles, and goes back, and circles", but first the *Kav* in general, and it does so through the first circle, the *machshava kduma*, the *Malchus* of the line. There are two wills. The simple will is one with the Essence; the decided will inside it, the *glif glifu*, settles how everything will be, the way a man is born with a taste for a red car or a baroque house, and yet it is no separate decision, "as if it were not there". So *tehiru ila'a* is above *klal* and *prat*, and to call G-d "looking and seeing in one glance" is *avoda zara*. The second will, after the *tzimtzum*, is the *ratzon kadum*: "I want a car", which already holds the steering wheel, as the house holds the kitchen and the sink. It comes down as the will to emanate, the architect, the draftsman and the contractor, to the last nail. But what it wanted was only the end: the man at his *Shabbos* table with his wife, the schmaltz herring and the vodka.

terms.gloss: an encompassing light; the first circle is the general makif of all four worlds equally

the lower purity: the first makif of the Kav after the tzimtzum, the general will for the whole building
the short line, in some places before even the machshava kduma, still called stima d'chol stimin

the impression after the tzimtzum: the letters of the glif glifu without the light, copied into the machshava kduma
a reversing seal: the glif glifu turned over into the reshimu, which stamped the machshava kduma
a dwelling, a home; what a home is depends on what you are

the beginning of the line; the ratzon kadum is called it and also comes after it

sections.title: Before the details: the Kav as the hiyuli of everything, taught through its first circle
sections.summary: The chapter sets out to explain the circles of the *Kav*, but first the *Kav* in general: the *hiyuli* of everything down to the end of *Asiya*. He explains it through the first circle, the *machshava kduma*, which is the *Malchus* of the line, and which the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures" is really about.

phrases.he: (טז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו וחוט זה,
איך שיש בו בחינת מקיפים ופנימיים
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
מתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: it's *misagel*, and then it goes back, another line from that *igul* down, and then it's again *misagel*

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)
ובחינת מקיף ועיגול הראשון הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה כו',
והוא בחינת המקיף הכללי שמקיף לד' עולמות דאבי''ע בשווה
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים

blocks.text: The particulars of the *Kav*: its encompassing and inner lights. It is *misagel v'chozer umisagel*: it circles, a line goes back down from the *igul* (circle), and it circles again. The first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, is the general *makif* of all four worlds of *ABYA* equally.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים כללות ענין הקו הזה,
phrases.en: but first let's understand what the general *inyan* of the *Kav* is

phrases.he: איך שהוא בחינת היולי כללי לכל הסתעפות המשכות פרטיים הרבה שמסתעפים ממנו עד סוף העשיה כו'
phrases.en: all kinds of things branch out all the way down to the end of *Asiya*; it is all from this line, it's the *hiyuli* for everything

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: But first, the general *inyan* (matter) of the *Kav*: everything branches out from this line down to the end of *Asiya*; it is the *hiyuli* for everything.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע בענין מחשבה כללית

blocks.text: He promised to explain the line, but he explains the first circle, the *machshava kduma* (primordial thought). He often calls it the line, because it is the end of the line, its *Malchus* (kingship).

They are not always one. In places the *kav katzar* (short line) is before the *machshava kduma* and is called *stima d'chol stimin* (most hidden of all), while the *machshava kduma* is *Atika Stima'a* (the hidden Ancient One). Here "the line" means the *machshava kduma*, because its *Keser* (crown) comes out from *Malchus* of the line, the end of its end: the little line, the *kav hamida* (line of measure), from whose *Malchus* only ten points come out.

phrases.he: שבמחשבה זו הכללית צופה ומביט עד סוף כל הדורות
בסקירה א'
(ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו מה שבידיעת עצמו יודע את כל הנבראים
כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: The general thought sees to the end of all generations in one glance: the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself He knows all creatures". So the *Rambam* is not speaking of before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), but of the kabbalistic *yichuda tata'a* (lower unity).

The earlier Kabbala books usually call *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus* (the levels of *Keser*) the *Atzmus* (Essence), and later he too counts them part of it. The *Atzmus* here is higher than *Yachid* (the first of the three levels), higher even than the *Maor* (source of light); some places stretch it down to the *gufa d'malka* (body of the King), the outside of the *Atzmus*. You have to know what they mean.
Most people take the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself" as *mamash* the self. It is the *machshava kduma*.

sections.title: The first will: the simple will in the Essence, with the decided will inside it
sections.summary: The simple will is one with the Essence; it is not even called a thought or a will. Within it is the decided will, the *glif glifu*, where it is already settled how each thing will be done; and still it is neither a *klal* nor a *prat*.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע שיש ב' מיני רצון
א' רצון הפשוט שבעצמות שנכלל בעצמותו ממש,
שלא נקרא עדיין בשם בחינת מחשבה ורצון כללי
phrases.en: as a matter of fact, it's not even called a *machshava* and *ratzon* altogether

phrases.he: כי מתאחד עדיין בעצמותו ממש

blocks.text: Two kinds of will. The first is the simple will in His Essence *mamash*, not even called thought and will: as in chapter 10, we say it is there only because we can't say it isn't.

phrases.he: כמו גם שהוחלט רצון זה כבר בעצמו
phrases.en: He already decided exactly how it's going to be done

phrases.he: איך לעשות דבר חסד פלוני
או איך לדבר ולחשוב אותו
או להשכיל שכל פרטי
או להיות לו רצון ותענוג בדבר כו'

blocks.text: The second level is the *ratzon hamuchlat* (decided will), the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving); *muchlat* is from *hachlata*, decision. **He already decided exactly how it's going to be done**, which kindness to do: the decision of the external.
It too has *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*: how to speak, think, conceive or delight. Even once made, the decision has to come from the Essence itself.

phrases.he: הגם שמתחבר רצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון בדבר הפרטי
אבל נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: it doesn't really come out, and does not actually have anything to do with the thing, even though the thing really comes out of it

phrases.he: ועל כן אין בו עדיין בחינת כלל ופרט כו'
phrases.en: there really is not a *klal*, not a *prat* there

blocks.text: It connects to the will's spreading into the thing, yet stays hidden in His Essence: it doesn't come out and has nothing to do with the thing, though the thing comes from it.

So it has no *klal* (whole) and *prat* (particular) yet, though you must also say it has both, even the particulars. Some think this makes the Essence a *klal*; but a real *klal* means the particulars are not there yet, which can't be said of the Essence.

sections.title: The composite will: "I want a car" holds every particular
sections.summary: Only when the decided will comes to an actual deed does it come out as *klal* and *prat*: one general thought, the *ratzon kadum*, a copy of the *glif glifu* through the *reshimu*, which holds the whole deed in one glance and then divides into particular wills, each encompassing the next like a wheel within a wheel. This is the composite will.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זה עולה רצון זה שהוחלט אצלו לבוא לידי מעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: when he decides to actually do it

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מהעלמו לגלוי
phrases.en: then it goes to revelation

phrases.he: אז יבוא הרצון בבחינת כלל ופרט,
phrases.en: then it comes in a way of a *klal* and *prat*

phrases.he: דהיינו מחשבה כללית שכוללת כל ענין המעשה מראש לסוף
phrases.en: meaning just, I want a car, and it includes everything

phrases.he: בסקירה א'

blocks.text: When He decides to act, it comes to revelation as *klal* and *prat*: first a *klal*, a general thought that includes the whole deed from beginning to end in one glance.
So with any will that comes to deed. And this whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent), which looks to us like everything, is by the *Aibershter* (the One Above) one little decision.

blocks.title: A man decides to buy a car
blocks.text: A man decides to buy a car: the will for a car was already in his simple will before the decision.

The decided will did not come out of the simple one; up there you can no more divide them than speak of *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, or ten *sefiros*. The decision comes out at some point, so it had to be there, and we call it decided. Only coming out is it *klal* and *prat*.

blocks.title: The red car
blocks.text: Coming out, it is one particular: buy the car. Even its kind and color follow a taste he already had, a predilection for a red car. He was born like that.

By the *Aibershter* there is no definition at all. A soul has ten *sefiros* mixed differently in each person, and that mix, his character, is already in his soul. Still, the taste you call his decided will is part of his simple will: that's the way he is, with no decision to make.
Since that's the way he is, it comes out at some point as a decision, and the *ratzon kadum* (preceding will) comes out as one thought including everything: I want a car.

The *machshava kduma* is a *tzimtzum* of the *glif glifu*, through the *reshimu* (impression): letters with the light gone out. One who can read them, like the *mashpia* (giver), finds the whole light in them; to anyone else they mean nothing. These letters were copied into the *machshava kduma*.
So it is called *Atika*: *atik* is a copy, as in *ha'atka*. It also means old, and removed, as in *ma'atik harim*, "he uproots mountains".

blocks.title: The printing press
blocks.text: The copy is not the original letters. The *glif glifu* is a *chosam hamis'hapech* (reversing seal): it turned over into the letters of the *reshimu*, which stamped those of the *machshava kduma*, as a printing press stamps a book. A different *metzius* (existence) of letters, but an exact copy: the same *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule).

blocks.title: A home, by a man and by a squirrel
blocks.text: It comes generally, like the will for a car. The Torah's *mashal* is a home: the *Aibershter* wanted a *dira* (dwelling) in the lower worlds. What a home is depends what you are: for a person a house, for a squirrel a hole in a tree.

blocks.title: A car with a steering wheel?
blocks.text: It comes out as one thing: a car. Ask him if it will have a steering wheel: of course. But did he think of a steering wheel when he decided? No, just a car; yet it included every particular, steering wheel, seats, windows, engine. That is the whole deed in one glance: **I want a car, and it includes everything**.

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצונות פרטיים
ולכל רצון שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and each *ratzon* has its own *sechel* and *middos*

phrases.he: ובאין זה אחר זה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: they come one after the other, with *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: זה עליון מקיף לתחתון,
phrases.en: one is higher and *makif* on that one

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך האופן כו'
phrases.en: like a wheel inside of a wheel

blocks.text: Then it divides into particular wills, the color, the shape, the engine, each with its own *sechel* (intellect) and *middos* (emotions).

blocks.title: The house, the kitchen and the sink
blocks.text: They come one after another, the higher encompassing the lower. His basic *mashal* is a house. You want a house, so you want a kitchen? Of course. A kitchen means a sink, and the sink should have a hole in the bottom? "Of course! If you have a sink, you have to have a hole in the bottom."

Each will includes more particular ones: the house is a general will to the kitchen, the kitchen to what is in it, and on down. A very physical *mashal* of *hishtalshelus*: the higher *makif* on the lower, a wheel within a wheel.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא רצון המורכב
phrases.en: it's called *ratzon hamurkav*

phrases.he: שיש בו כלל ופרט
phrases.en: it's made up of particulars

blocks.text: This composite will, the *ratzon hamurkav*, is made of particulars, *klal* and *prat*; the simple will is made of nothing.

sections.title: The analogy of the man who builds a great house: a taste settled long before, then the plan from klal to prat
sections.summary: A man's taste in houses is in him before he ever decides to build: decided, yet not a separate decision, "as if it were not there". When he comes to build, it comes first as one general picture of the whole house, and then divides, will within will, down to the last detail.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע,
אדם שרוצה לבנות בנין גדול
כפי הרצון שהוחלת מכבר אצלו להיות בו אופנים מיוחדים דוקא
phrases.en: it's already in his inner *hachlata* that it should be in a certain way

phrases.he: שאותו הרצון שהוחלט אצלו מכבר,
הגם שהוא בא במדה ותענוג מיוחד באופן כך וכך,
phrases.en: he has a particular taste, even before it came out to anything

phrases.he: וממילא בשכל ומדות בא בשיעור ומדה כו',
phrases.en: so since it's already in a certain way, *mimeila* it has to have, in *sechel* and *middos*, a *shiur* and *midda*, since the *shiur* and *midda* is the whole thing

phrases.he: אך כל זה הוא השיעור וההחלט שבעצמותו עדיין,
ונכלל בעצמו
והיה כלא היה כו'
phrases.en: it's like it doesn't really exist

blocks.text: A man who wants a great building already has, inside, a particular taste for how it should be, so it comes with a measure in intellect and emotions, the measure being the whole thing. But it is still within him, *hayah k'lo hayah* (as if it were not): his taste, not a separate decision.

blocks.title: A modern house or the Addams Family house
blocks.text: One man's inner image of a house is very modern, everything square; another's is the Addams Family house with gargoyles (baroque, a listener supplies). Know the person and you know what house he'd buy.
That is no actual decision; the *ratzon hamuchlat* is part of the *ratzon hapashut*. The decision outside had to be inside first, but there it was no separate thing, as if not there.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זמן באה מחשבה זו לבא למעשה,
ניכר בו התחלקות אותן אופנים שונים ממש
שכבר הוחלט אצלו
בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: and every particular little part

blocks.text: Only later is it acted on; the decision was decided before he made it, a predisposition for a certain house or car.

blocks.title: "She would love this dress"
blocks.text: Well, women go shopping. Someone who knows a person well says, "She would love this dress." She never saw it; how does he know? Because he knows her. So there is already a decision in her for this dress, though she might never see it: a will and a delight, already decided, that never came to action.

sensitivity.reason: Opens with a passing generalisation, "women go shopping".

blocks.text: Only in action is it divided, exactly as decided in **every particular little part**: which kitchen, which bathroom.

phrases.he: רק שמתחלה בא הרצון הזה בדרך כלל
phrases.en: it comes in a general way: just, I want a house

phrases.he: שיהיה לו בנין בציור כך וכך
phrases.en: it's for this particular house; it's like a baroque house or a modern house already

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצון פרטי לכל ענין פרטי
phrases.en: and then, only afterwards (first he has to have the general *ratzon*), the general *ratzon* can divide into all the particular *pratim*

blocks.text: First it comes in general: just **I want a house**. Even that is already a baroque or a modern house; only afterwards does the general will divide into its particulars.

phrases.he: ויורד ובא בסדר והדרגה
phrases.en: it comes down *b'seder hadraga*

phrases.he: מכלל הראשון שכולל הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: from the first *klal*, that includes the whole house in one *skira*

phrases.he: לפרט רצון שהוא נקרא כלל לגבי רצונות המסתעפים ממנו
עד שבא אל רצון ושכל פרטי היותר אחרון שבסוף מעשה בכלות הכל כו'
phrases.en: till he comes to the final particular thing at the end of the *maaseh*

phrases.he: ודי למבין.
phrases.en: and this is enough to understand

blocks.text: It comes down by steps from the first *klal*, the whole house in one *skira* (glance): he says only "a house", and the entire house appears in his mind at once. From it comes a particular will that is a *klal* to those branching from it, like the kitchen, also in one glance, and so lower and lower.
Down to the last particular at the end of the deed. Now the *meshalim* (analogies) must change: above, it is not so physical.

sections.title: The nimshal above: tehiru ila'a is beyond even "one glance"
sections.summary: What He measured in Himself in *tehiru ila'a* is the decided will within the simple will: it never comes out of the Essence. So it is above *klal* and *prat*, and above even "looking and seeing in one glance"; to call G-d that is *avoda zara*.

phrases.he: והנמשל מכל זה יובן למעלה
בהפרש שבין בחינת טהירו עילאה ובין בחינת טהירו תתאה שלאחר הצמצום
דמה ששיער בעצמו בכח בטהירו עילאה כו'
הוא כמו ההחלט ברצון הפשוט שבעצמות הנזכר לעיל
שעדיין לא בא כלל לבחינת התפשטות חוץ מן העצמות עדיין
וגם שיתחבר מרצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון שאחר כך,
phrases.en: really it is connected, that's where it comes from

phrases.he: מכל מקום נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמות דאור אין סוף

blocks.text: The *nimshal* (what it stands for): what He measured in Himself in potential, in *tehiru ila'a*, is like the decision in the simple will of the Essence. The will's spreading afterwards comes from it, yet it stays hidden in the Essence of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: ועל כן למעלה הוא מבחינת כלל
phrases.en: it's even higher than a *klal*

phrases.he: להיות נקרא צופה ומביט בסקירה א' כו'.
phrases.en: you can't say about it *tzofeh umabit b'skira achas*

blocks.text: So it is above a *klal*: not a *klal*, not a *prat*, not even not a *klal* and *prat*, and not "looking and seeing in one glance".
Some think they know what G-d is: "looking and seeing in one glance." That's *avoda zara* (idolatry): He is higher than that, not looking at all. That's just the way He is.

sections.title: The second will, after the tzimtzum: the ratzon kadum, and what it really wanted
sections.summary: After the *tzimtzum* the decided will comes to spread out: that is the *Kav*, whose first *makif* is the *tehiru tata'a*, the will that includes all wills. It comes down as the will to emanate, the will to create, down to the last deed; but what it wanted was only the end, the way a man building a house wants only to sit at his *Shabbos* table with his wife.

phrases.he: אך הרצון הב' הוא אחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
שעולה רצון הפשוט המוחלט שבעצמות לבא לידי בחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: when it comes to spread out, that he actually is going to get a house

phrases.he: הוא בחינת הקו וחוט ההיולי
שכולל כל המשכות פרטיות שבו מראשו לסופו כנזכר לעיל
ובחינת מקיף הראשון שבו הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה,
שזהו כמשל רצון הכללי לבנין גדול כולל כל מה שבפרטיו מראשו לסופו בבת א'
ואחר כך מתחלק בו בסדר והדרגה מכלל לפרט
על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like we explained before

blocks.text: The second will is after the *tzimtzum*, when the decided will arises to spread out: he actually is going to get a house. That is the *hiyuli* power that includes all. Its first *makif*, *tehiru tata'a*, is like the will for a great building, all its particulars at once, which then divides by steps.

phrases.he: והיינו כמו כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט ההיולי לבא לגלוי דוקא,
היה כולל כל פרטי הרצונות
והוא הרצון הכולל כולם,
ונקרא רצון קדום לכל מה שבא אחריו
ואחר כך בא רצון זה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: this *ratzon klal*, the *ratzon kadum*, that's coming into the *pratim*

phrases.he: כמו הרצון להאציל
ובו כלול עשר ספירות בכל פרטיהם
ועדיין הכל בהעלם
phrases.en: this *prat*, the *ratzon l'ha'atzil*, is still *b'helem*

phrases.he: עד שבא לידי גלוי שהוא כשנאצל האור בבחינת האצילות כו'
phrases.en: it only comes in *gilui* when the actual *Atzilus* of the thing

blocks.text: When the simple *hiyuli* will arose to reveal itself, it included all particular wills: the *ratzon kadum* to all after it. Then comes the particular will to emanate, in which the ten *sefiros* are included. (He corrects the reading: "in which are included", a *beis*, not a *kaf*.)
The will to emanate stays hidden until the actual *Atzilus*, its four levels, comes about.

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא יש מאין כו'
ובו שכל ומדות כו'
עד הרצון היותר אחרון
שהוא כל אשר חפץ עשה כו',
סוף הכל
phrases.en: the end of everything

blocks.text: Then the will to create *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), down to the will for the last *Asiya*, which includes **the end of everything**.

Unlike the house, kitchen and sink, where the sink is not the main thing, here the main thing is *Asiya*; all else, *Atzilus* too, is a *derech ma'avar* (way of passing through). He wants the end thing.

First the will to emanate. His will for a house is in his decided will, since a man without a house is not a man. And he wants a home: *beiso zo ishto*, his house is his wife, a place to live with her.
The real thing he wants is a wife. As with Lavan, the verse names the other tents, and Rachel's it calls the house of Yaakov.

blocks.title: The swimming pool that is a will to swim
blocks.text: The will to emanate is still within him, since *Atzilus* is not outside him: what he wants from a house. There the swimming pool is the will to swim, the kitchen the will to eat his way.

To be *ma'atzil* (emanate) is to draw out of himself the house's *middos*, his own: a *sechel* person gets a *sechel* house, a physical person a tennis court, really his desire to be a certain way. Clarifying his wills is the house's *Atzilus*.

blocks.title: The architect: Beriya
blocks.text: Next, *Beriya*: the architect, who takes from *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*. For a perfect house he must get out of the man what he was *mesha'er* (measuring) inside, his will and delight in a house. Big parties, or sitting alone with books? Books mean a den and a library; entertaining, a big kitchen and a banquet room.

*Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the *dibur* (speech), becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*, the will that gives the architect all he will design. Telling him what he wants, the man is telling him about himself, the *gufa d'malka*: who he is, what he desires. A man who likes muscles wants a weightlifting room, but in *Atzilus* it is the muscles of the king. The kitchen is his stomach: each part of the house comes from a perception of himself or of his body, the kitchen, like the bathroom, from the digestive tract.

blocks.question: Isn't the self-perception Adam Kadmon? Aren't we in Atzilus already, and isn't the machshava kduma Adam Kadmon?
blocks.text: No, there's no self-perception yet: this is all in the *machshava kduma*, before the architect. The *machshava kduma* is not *Adam Kadmon* (primordial man) but before it, its *Keser*. There is no will for *Atzilus* yet; the house's *Atzilus* is just included in his thought, within himself.
He first calls the architect's concept *Yetzira*, but it is *Beriya*, something from nothing: before, it was a person, not a house; now it is a house in the shape of a person.

blocks.title: The perfect chair
blocks.text: Or a chair, whose *etzem* (essence) is a *tachas* (behind), the man himself: to make the perfect chair you must know his measurements, behind, back, arms. Like the *shiur koma*, a listener says; that, he answers, is *Adam Kadmon*, and this is before it.
*Yetzira* is the draftsman. Not yet a house, but *Yetzira* is making the form: drafting the plan created in *Beriya* into an actual form.

*Asiya* is the contractor. *Keser* of *Yetzira* comes from *Malchus* of *Beriya*, the architect telling the draftsman his idea; the final blueprint, *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, goes to the contractor as *Keser* of *Asiya*. Down to the last nail, it is all in the *machshava kduma*.
Then the house is built, and when he furnishes it and moves in with his wife, that is the *machshava kduma* itself, the real desire: not *Asiya*, but its product.

blocks.title: "Here's your money, get out of here"
blocks.text: Now we don't need a contractor no more: "Here's your money, get out of here," his wife is coming any minute. So the final product is in a way not part of the *hishtalshelus*.

blocks.title: Schmaltz herring and vodka on Shabbos
blocks.text: Yet it is the real *machshava kduma*, which was not even the house but *Shabbos*: guests, candles lit, wine on the table, schmaltz herring and vodka.

The *machshava kduma* included the whole process, but he didn't think of *Atzilus* down to *Asiya*; he thought straight to the end: a home, his wife. A home is sitting with his wife, not walls: for a squirrel a hole in a tree, for a bird a nest; a *dira* for him and his family. That is the end of the deed, **the end of everything**.

phrases.he: וכל פרטים הללו נכללו ברצון הקדום
phrases.en: they're already included in the *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת השפעה על כל פנים אחר הצמצום

blocks.text: All this is included in the *ratzon kadum*, which comes as *hashpa'a* (giving forth) after the *tzimtzum*; yet it is not really *hashpa'a*. It is still for himself, not even for the house but for his delight in the home.

sections.title: The beginning of the Kav and the first circle: circle within circle, down to a slice of pizza
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is called both the beginning of the *Kav* and the circle after it, because its *Keser* comes from the *Malchus* of the beginning of the *Kav*. From each circle a line goes down to the next circle, which is again a *ratzon kadum* to what is inside it: that is "it circles, and goes back and circles".

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ראשית הקו כו',
phrases.en: and that is the beginning of the line

phrases.he: והיינו עיגול הראשון שאחר המשכת ראשית הקו ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is the *igul harishon* (the first circle), which is after the *reishis hakav*

phrases.he: שנקרא מקיף כללי לכללות כל הד' עולמות דאבי''ע, שמקיף אותם בשוה
שנקרא מחשבה כללית שצופה ומביט בסקירה א' מראש לסוף הכל כו'

blocks.text: It is **the beginning of the line**, and the first circle, after the beginning of the line: two opposites, and again it depends which *Kav*, the first *hiyuli* line or the next one, reaching to the end of *Adam Kadmon*, which is its beginning. It is the general *makif* of all four worlds, the thought that sees everything in one glance.

phrases.he: וזהו ביאור ענין כללי לכללות ענין הקו הזה

blocks.text: He calls this the explanation of the *Kav*, but the chapter is all about the *machshava kduma*, which he calls the *Kav*; and in one sentence the *ratzon kadum* is both the *reishis hakav* and after it.

The answer: the *ratzon kadum* is after the *reishis hakav*, but its *Keser* comes from the last of the line's ten points, its *Malchus*: really from how *Malchus* of *Malchus* becomes *Keser* of the next rung. This *Kav*, from the *machshava kduma* down, includes all the worlds as a general *makif*.

phrases.he: ופרטי אופניו במה שמתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
יובן לפי אופן משל הנזכר לעיל
וכמו שיתבאר בסמוך בעזרת ה׳ ודי למבין:

blocks.text: Circling, going back and circling: the going back and circling, it seems, he never explained, but he did, with the four worlds. From the *tzimtzum* through the *reshimu* the line comes to the first circle, the *machshava kduma*; from it a line comes to the next particular, again a circle, the general will for what is inside it, a wheel in a wheel. So each lower circle is a *machshava kduma* to what is inside it.

blocks.title: A piece of pizza
blocks.text: Every will is like that, down to pizza. "I'd like a piece of pizza" includes his wallet, car key, the drive, joking with the guy at the pizza place. But he wanted the end of it all: in the *ratzon kadum* it was a will for a pizza.
So each particular will is a *ratzon kadum* to all inside it, in one glance: circling, going back and circling, as the analogy will explain.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does he say the chapter, which promises to explain the *Kav*, is really explaining the *machshava kduma*, and how can that still be called the line?
What is the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures" really talking about, and why does it matter what the books of Kabbala call the *Atzmus*?
How can there be a decided will inside the simple will, when there is no *klal* and no *prat* in it? Use the man with the predilection for a red car.
What does the steering wheel show about the general thought, and what does the house, the kitchen and the sink add to it?
Why is it *avoda zara* to say that G-d is "looking and seeing in one glance"?
In the house analogy of the four worlds, what are *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and what was the *machshava kduma* really for?

notes.text: Class 014 reads line 13 twice: once straight after line 12 (w1525-1555), then again at w2699 after the long explanation. Lines 12 and 13 are one passage, so the whole explanation sits under both.
He cites "a person who doesn't have a house is not a person" with "it says" and no source; left as he said it. The reviewer may want to check the wording of the saying he has in mind.
On Lavan's search he first says "the tent of Leah", then corrects himself to Rachel; the block gives the corrected version. (Rashi on Genesis 31:33 says Yaakov's tent was Rachel's.)

Class 024 w1110-1259 is a back-and-forth with no speaker labels; the split between the student's question (self-perception as Adam Kadmon, "Atzilus already", "so the machshava kduma is Adam Kadmon") and his answers is my reading. He says the machshava kduma is "before Adam Kadmon" and also "Keser of Adam Kadmon"; both are kept.
Class 024 w1260-1303: he begins "what is Yetzira? when the architect came out with a concept", then calls that a Beriya; Yetzira proper comes at w1446. The block says he puts it right.
Class 014 line 30: he reads "the general hiyuli power" where the text has "the Kav v'chut, the hiyuli"; the phrase follows the text, the block what he said.
Class 024 line 36: the reading is corrected from "and so on" to "in which are included" ("It's a beis, not a kaf"); it is not clear whether he or the reader first misread.

Several listener interjections ("Baroque", "the dibur", "like the shiur koma", "my wife", "in the same sentence") have no speaker label; they are given as a listener's where the next sentence answers them, otherwise folded into his words.

The aside at 014 w4141-4203 ("That's avoda zara") is not flagged: it is said of a theological idea (that G-d is "looking and seeing in one glance"), not of people or of a practice, and a public edition of a Chassidus class can print it as it stands.

terms is trimmed to 12 key terms; the incidental words (mafrish, mesha'er, ma'atzil, tachas, beiso zo ishto, ha'atka, ma'atik harim, derech ma'avar, hachlata, shiur koma and others) are glossed inline at first use only. None of them is in translit.json, except ma'atzil, added when the chapters were merged.
